correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge4\) and gain \(\kappa>0\), the grounded Laplacian is SPD. Its block inverse trace is \(F_i=s_A+s_B+(s_Bt_A+s_At_B)/(1-s_As_B)\). All three differences \(F_2-F_0\), \(F_0-F_1\), \(F_2-F_1\) have explicitly displayed polynomial numerators and positive denominators. For \(4\le m\le10\) the polynomial signs and ordered exact rational root brackets yield every claimed interval and transition tie; for \(m\ge11\) \(P_{01}\) is everywhere positive (coefficient/discriminant proof), and \(P_{21}\) has exactly one positive root (Descartes rule and endpoint signs). No unproved root ordering or finite enumeration is needed. A package-local exact-rational inverter independently checks 81 direct matrix traces and 96 parameter pairs for cleared-denominator identities. These tests are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prior work establishes the finite-gain grounded-Laplacian inverse-trace objective and broad algorithms, but inspected sources do not state the exact all-integer four-leader \(K_{2,m}\) phase classification. The result is not an isolated numerical example: it separates three regimes at exactly \(m=9,10\), two regimes at \(m=7,8\) and \(m\ge11\), and one regime at \(m=4,5,6\) with provable algebraic transitions. Existing generic formulas reduce computation to an optimization objective but do not imply the sign comparison and size classification without new deductions. Historical priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The problem is a natural finite-gain sensor/leader allocation on the smallest nonsymmetric complete bipartite family with three leader-orbit possibilities. A full exact integer-size and positive-gain phase diagram supplies quantitative design choices and all degeneracies. The exceptional 2-to-0-to-1 transition at precisely \(m=9,10\) is structurally counterintuitive; proving its isolation for an infinite family is a non-routine optimization boundary, beyond calculating a known inverse or listing a few cases.
